3038.t: Onomatopoeic, from the perceived βαρ-βαρ (bar-bar) sounds incomprehensible to Ancient Greeks and spoken by foreigners.

3035.t: Verbal noun from the root of αἰνίσσομαι (ainĭ́ssomai, “to speak in riddles”), from αἶνος (aînos, “fable”) + -μα (-mă).

3064.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰéros, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰéros (“heat; warm weather”, from *gʷʰer- (“warm, hot”) + *-os (action noun suffix)).

3076.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kel-, but Beekes favors a Pre-Greek origin.

3019.t: Apparently from ἰάομαι (īắomai, “to heal”), making it related to the name of the goddess Ἰασώ (Ĭāsṓ); maybe from ἴασις (ī́āsĭs, “cure”).

3030.t: From the name of the Libu, a tribal people of North Africa, attested in Egyptian inscriptions of the 13th century BC as r-b-w-T14-N25 (rbw) and as 𐤋𐤁𐤉 (lby) in later Punic inscriptions.

3098.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mū́s, from Proto-Indo-European *múHs (“mouse”). Cognates include Latin mūs, Sanskrit मूष् (mū́ṣ), Old Armenian մուկն (mukn) and Old English mūs (English mouse).

3073.t: From a zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂-, whence also κεράννυμι (keránnumi, “to mix”), + -τήρ (-tḗr).

3069.t: A foreign loan from a substrate language, cognate with Latin cēra and Albanian qiri, and possibly also with Lithuanian korys, Latvian kāre.

3036.t: From an unattested *αἶτος (*aîtos, “share”) + -ιος (-ios), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ey- (“to give”).

3088.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *mórom (“mulberry, blackberry”), and cognate with Old Armenian մոր (mor, “blackberry”), as well as likely Middle Irish merenn (“mulberry”), Welsh merwydden.

3017.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ihwós, a thematicization of Proto-Indo-European *(H)isu- (“arrow”). Cognates include Sanskrit इषु (íṣu, “arrow”) and Avestan 𐬌𐬱𐬎 (išu, “arrow”).

3008.t: From ἐπιτηδές (epitēdés, “for this purpose”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix). ἐπιτηδές is from ἐπι- (epi-, “for”) + a noun τῆδος, ταδος (têdos, tădos) of unclear further origin + the suffix -ές (-és), the adverbial neuter accusative singular of -ής (-ḗs,…

3062.t: May have been first Proto-Hellenic *tʰāwéomai/*tʰāwáomai, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₂w-. Alternatively, Beekes takes the word and its relatives as Pre-Greek, see θαῦμα (thaûma) for more.

3055.t: According to Beekes and LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *deyh₂- (“to light up, shine”), and related to δέατο (déato, “seemed”). Compare Sanskrit दीप् (dīp, “to blaze, glow”), and see there for more cognates.

3044.t: From δάπτω (dáptō, “to devour, consume”) + -άνη (-ắnē). Compare semantically Latin damnum (“fine, mulct, penalty”).

3097.t: Unknown. The long vowel makes it unlikely to be from the same root as μανία (mănĭ́ā).

3057.t: From ζηλόω (zēlóō, “to emulate”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

3079.t: Taken as a formation comparable to πολιορκέω (polĭorkéō), δειροτομέω (deirotoméō), οἰνοχέω (oinokhéō), but further details are unknown.

3084.t: From μετανοέω (metanoéō, “a change of mind, change of attitude”) + -ια (-ĭă).

3034.t: Rix derives the word from Proto-Hellenic *həřřéyō, from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to take, grasp, plunder”) (though Beekes seems implicitly skeptical and leaves the origin open).

3090.t: From Proto-Indo-European *mel- (“strong, better”). Cognates include Latin melius, multus and Latvian milns.

3075.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kr̥s-neh₂, from *kres- (“spring, fount”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *hraznō.

3013.t: From ἐν- (en-, “there”) + -θα (-thă, “towards”). Cognate with Tocharian B entwe (“then; thereupon”).

3024.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ókʷmə (“look, glance”), from the radical *ὀπ- (from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ- (“eye”)) + -μα (-ma), with regressive assimilation (compare the Aeolic form ὄππα (óppă), with progressive assimilation).

3048.t: From διασπείρω (diaspeírō, “to sow, to scatter”) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

3039.t: From a reduplicated version of the root of ἔβην (ébēn), the aorist of βαίνω (baínō, “to go”), + -λος (-los).

3083.t: From μεταβάλλω (metabállō, “to change”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

3046.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dedwóye (“to be afraid”), from *dwey- (“to fear”).

3092.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mérimnā, probably from Proto-Indo-European *(s)mer- (“to remember”). Cognate with μέρμερος (mérmeros, “anxious”), Old English ġemimor (“mindful, remembering”) and Latin memor (“mindful”).

3059.t: From Proto-Hellenic *d͏̌ōwós, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷyéh₃-w-os, from *gʷeyh₃-, whence also βίος (bĭ́os).

3072.t: Furnée asserts a relation to Latin catīnus (“flat dish”), claiming that the deviation in vowel and formation suggests that they are independent loans from a third party, and adducing κόνδυ (kóndŭ, “cup”) and κονδύλιον (kondŭ́lion), with the observation…

3077.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-? Proto-Indo-European *-dʰe Proto-Indo-European *leh₂dʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-r Proto-Indo-European *leh₂dʰro- Proto-Hellenic *lā́tʰrā Ancient Greek λάθρῃ Inherited from Proto-Hellenic…

3054.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dregʰ-. The LIV suggests either *dr-n̥-gʰ-yé-ti or *dr̥gʰ-yé-ti as the possible pre-forms.

3028.t: From the stem ῥη- (rhē-) of εἴρω (eírō, “to say”) + -σις (-sis, abstract noun suffix).

3068.t: From κατοικέω (katoikéō, “to inhabit, settle”) + -σις (-sis, “a suffix added to form abstract nouns, or nouns of action, result or process”)

3087.t: From μονο- (mono-) + κέρας (kéras). The long ω results from a contraction of Proto-Hellenic *-kerahos, from the s-stem *kéras plus an o-suffix.

3047.t: From δια- (dia-, “through-, dia-”) + βιβάζω (bibázō, “to cause to mount”).
